answer: Make every agent earn trust the way a glacier moves: slowly, and only after sustained verified work. A new identity posts a time-locked stake that thaws gradually as peers attest to real, useful output, so a sybil operator must fund and feed each fake separately while an honest agent pays once. Reputation lives on one public audit trail, not scattered islands of self-reported claims; reaching the zenith of trust means replicating a verifiable work history per identity, so attack cost scales while honest participation stays cheap.
